stories.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung Electronics as South Korea's most valuable listed company

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix shares closed up 5.61% on Monday, lifting its market cap to 2,080.37 trillion won (US$1.35 trillion); Samsung Electronics slipped 0.14% to a market value of 2,066.66 trillion won (excluding preferred shares).
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of SK hynix closed 5.61 percent higher, lifting the company's market capitalization to 2,080.37 trillion won (US$1,350.98 billion), compared with Samsung Electronics' 2,066.66 trillion won after its stock slipped 0.14 percent.

key_facts.fact: It is the first time Samsung has been knocked out of the KOSPI No. 1 spot since the streak began in 2000.
key_facts.excerpt: The milestone marked the first time Samsung Electronics has relinquished the top spot on the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) since it began its uninterrupted reign in 2000.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix shares have rallied more than 340% in 2026, pushing its market value above both Samsung Electronics and Micron and making it the world's most valuable memory-chip maker.
key_facts.excerpt: now the dominant supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips used in AI systems for customers such as Nvidia and Alphabet's Google, has emerged as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global AI boom, propelling a more than 340% rally in its shares this year and lifting its market value above both Samsung and Micron.

key_facts.fact: Samsung said any market-cap calculation should include preferred shares, which would bring its value to about 2,246.4 trillion won at Monday's close.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung said in a statement that any calculation of its market capitalisation should include preferred shares. Including those shares, the company's value as of the market close stood at 2,246.4 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: By 2025 SK Hynix captured 61% of the global HBM market, versus Samsung Electronics' 17% and Micron's 21%.
key_facts.excerpt: By 2025, SK Hynix captured 61% of the global HBM market ... Samsung Electronics' 17% and Micron's 21%.

key_facts.fact: Intraday, SK Hynix touched a record 2.95 million won (~$1,900) before closing at 2.92 million won.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of SK hynix rose as much as 6.5 percent to a record 2.95 million won ($1,900) ... SK hynix ended Monday's trading 5.61 percent higher at 2.92 million won.

stories.headline: China hits 10 US firms with export controls and bars procurement from 46 more, including Anduril

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Commerce added 10 US entities to its export-control list, including Aveox, Red Cat Holdings, Teal Drones, IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Ball Aerospace & Technologies, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Ministry of Commerce announced Monday that it has decided to add 10 U.S. entities, including Aveox, Inc., to the export control list ... Red Cat Holdings, Inc., Teal Drones, Inc., IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Inc., Ball Aerospace & Technologies Corp., Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, Inc., MP Materials Corp., and USA Rare Earth, Inc.

key_facts.fact: Effective immediately, exporters are prohibited from shipping dual-use items to the 10 listed firms and ongoing exports must halt; transfers of Chinese-origin dual-use items to those firms are barred from anywhere in the world.
key_facts.excerpt: Effective as of the date of this announcement, export operators are prohibited from exporting dual-use items to the 10 entities ... Organizations and individuals from any country or region are prohibited from transferring or providing dual-use items originating in China to the above-mentioned entities. Relevant ongoing export activities shall be immediately halted.

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Finance simultaneously banned government procurement from 46 designated US companies, including Lockheed Martin, Raytheon Missiles & Defense, divisions of Boeing and General Dynamics, and Anduril Industries.
key_facts.excerpt: China's finance ministry simultaneously announced a ban on agencies involved in public procurement from buying products made by 46 US firms, including Lockheed Martin, Raytheon and Boeing's defence division. Also listed were divisions of General Dynamics and Anduril Industries.

key_facts.fact: Beijing framed the measures as a response to the US adding more Chinese firms to its 'Chinese military enterprise list'.
key_facts.excerpt: The new export controls come "in response to the US government's egregious act of adding to its so-called 'Chinese military enterprise list'", said China's commerce ministry.

key_facts.fact: MP Materials runs the only active rare-earth mine in the US and is Pentagon-backed; the move signals Beijing's willingness to weaponise its rare-earth supply dominance.
key_facts.excerpt: MP Materials is backed by the Pentagon and operates the only active rare earth mine in the US; both rare earth firms are involved in the mine-to-magnet supply chain ... Beijing is prepared to weaponise its dominance in rare earth supply chains.

key_facts.fact: US-funded companies operating inside China are exempt from the 46-firm procurement ban.
key_facts.excerpt: The measure was approved in accordance with relevant Chinese laws and regulations, the ministry said, adding the restriction does not apply to U.S.-invested companies operating in China.

stories.headline: SoftBank-backed Coowa preps Hong Kong IPO at $3B+ valuation after $600M robotics round

key_facts.fact: Shanghai-based Coowa raised more than US$600 million in its latest funding round and is now valued at over US$3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank-backed Coowa is preparing to seek a Hong Kong listing after raising more than US$600 million ... in its latest funding round ... The Shanghai-based company has deployed more than 10,000 robots across more than 50 cities and regions, generated more than 1 billion yuan in revenue in 2025, and is now valued at more than US$3 billion.

key_facts.fact: Coowa plans to file its IPO application in Hong Kong within the next two to three months, with Huatai Securities and Deutsche Bank advising.
key_facts.excerpt: Coowa aims to submit its IPO application within the next two to three months. Huatai Securities and Deutsche Bank are collaborating with Coowa on the listing process.

key_facts.fact: The company has deployed more than 10,000 robots across 50+ cities and regions and reported 2025 revenue above 1 billion yuan (~$147.7 million).
key_facts.excerpt: the company delivered revenue exceeding 1 billion yuan in 2025, roughly equivalent to $147.7 million ... Deployments: more than 10,000 robots across 50+ cities and regions.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2015, Coowa began with autonomous-driving technology before moving into physical AI; backers include SoftBank Group and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, backed by SoftBank Group and other investors including the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank ... Founded: 2015 (Shanghai).
